clips.title: The story
paras: "Falling With Style" is an introductory rite of passage for young Skyborne in Thendal Village. Offered atop the local watchtower by the mischievous Myriaal Mistwake, it challenges novices to test their innate slow-fall ability by leaping from the platform toward Rorian the Dayseeker below.

Perched high above Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Myriaal Mistwake invites young Skyborne to test their heritage through a game of daring. Rather than treating their innate magical gifts as sacred relics kept under strict restraint, Myriaal encourages newcomers to leap into the open air from the watchtower ledge. The purpose is practical as well as playful: mastering the instinctive art of walking upon air before life beyond the grove demands it in perilous situations.

The exercise serves as a vivid demonstration of two contrasting Skyborne attitudes. While Myriaal delights in sudden descents and startles onlookers for amusement, Rorian the Dayseeker embodies traditional caution. When novices glide down to land squarely before him, Rorian admonishes the reckless display, warning that thoughtlessly exhausting one's magical gifts can leave a traveler helpless when danger strikes. Even so, he concedes that controlled practice within the safety of the village has its place.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Well hello there, friend! Want to play a game?
All you've got to do is step up on that ledge... Then jump! Use your innate ability to walk on the air to slow your fall and see how far forward you can float.

The rules are made up and the points don't matter, but you get bonus points if you can land right in front of Rorian the Dayseeker and startle him! He won't like it but I'll certainly get a good laugh if you can get him all worked up! Hah!

clips.title: Progress
paras: Using your ability to walk on air can get you out of--and, well... Into--all kinds of trouble!

clips.title: Completion
paras: How many times do I need to tell Myriaal not to encourage others to make reckless usage of our skyborne gifts!
That being said, I suppose that a little bit of practice in the relative safety of the village is... Acceptable.
In the future I'd simply suggest you to use your ability judiciously. You do not want to exhaust your magic thoughtlessly and then not be able to use it when you truly need it.
